old: Use *hacerse*, *convertirse en*, *pasar de... a...*, *seguir* + gerund and other change expressions to describe development over time. The imperfect, present perfect and present can establish stages of change.
new: Spanish uses a different verb for different kinds of \"becoming\". *Ponerse* + adjective is a change of mood or state that can pass: Mi amiga se puso muy triste. *Volverse* + adjective is a deeper change: Mi vecino se volvió muy serio. *Hacerse* + noun is a change you reach by effort or with time: Un amigo mío se hizo médico. *Quedarse* + adjective is the result of something: Mi amiga se quedó sola. You also use *convertirse en* + noun and *pasar de ser … a ser …* for bigger changes, and you know *seguir* + gerund from A2 Unit 28.
why: Screen did not teach the unit's skill verbs-of-change (ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse): it listed hacerse/convertirse en/pasar de/seguir without any of the four; rewritten, italics fixed
examples for ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse

old: Describe both the starting point and the direction of change when possible.
new: Choose the verb by the kind of change: *ponerse* and *quedarse* for a state that can pass, *volverse* for a deeper change, *hacerse* for a change you reach by effort or with time.
why: tip taught nothing new; now guides the choice of verb

old: Contrast past and present with *antes*, en *aquella* *época*, *actualmente*, hoy en día, todavía and ya. Use imperfecto for past situations and present or present perfect for current states and changes.
new: You know the imperfect and the present perfect for change over time from B1 Unit 9. Here you add the time markers that name the two periods: *antes* and *en aquella época* for the past, *actualmente* and *hoy en día* for the present, and *en comparación con* to compare them.
why: Screen presented the imperfect / present perfect contrast (B1 Unit 9) as new; italics broken ('en *aquella* *época*')

old: *Todavía* and *ya* work as a pair: *todavía* says a past situation continues, while *ya* marks that something has now changed — together they let you pinpoint exactly when a shift happened.
new: Use *todavía* for what has not changed and *ya no* for what has: Todavía vivo aquí, pero ya no trabajo en esa oficina.
why: tip said todavía/ya 'work as a pair... pinpoint exactly when a shift happened' (not what they do); one natural sentence

old: Use the future tense, *ir a* + infinitive and probability expressions to make predictions. Use probably, perhaps and similar expressions to show how certain a prediction is.
new: You know the future from A2 Unit 19, *ir a* + infinitive from A1 Unit 25 and *es posible que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 25. Here you use them with *probablemente* and *es probable que* to show how sure a prediction is: the future for what you expect, *es probable que* + subjunctive for what is likely.
why: Screen presented known future / ir a / subjunctive-doubt as new; italics

old: Use es *necesario* *que*, es *importante* que, *hace* *falta* que and other necessity expressions with the subjunctive. Use the infinitive when the subject remains general or the same.
new: You know *es importante que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27 and necessity + subjunctive from B1 Unit 35. Here you use *es necesario que*, *es importante que* and *hace falta que* to say what has to change, and the infinitive when no particular person is named.
why: Screen presented necessity + subjunctive (A2 Unit 27, B1 Unit 35, B1 Unit 39) as new; italics ('es *necesario* *que*')

old: Compare the last example with the others: es *necesario* *mejorar* el sistema uses the infinitive because no specific subject is named, while que la *sociedad* *se* *adapte* names one and switches to the subjunctive.
new: Compare: Es necesario mejorar el sistema (no person named, infinitive) and Es necesario que la sociedad se adapte (a person named, subjunctive).
why: tip had stray italic runs on single words

old: Discussing change requires description of the past and present, prediction of future developments, evaluation of what needs to change and explanation of possible challenges and opportunities.
new: You know every part of this discussion from the unit: the imperfect and present perfect with time markers, the future and *probablemente*, necessity + subjunctive and the verbs of change. Now put them together to say what changed, what will happen and what has to change.
why: no recap: all of it was taught in lessons 1-4
the four verbs of the skill were not in the vocabulary list
story words in no list: huérfano, capitán, batalla (used in the reading items)
